methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting Hampton Roads residents signal grassroots capability-building outside the NoVA corridor, indicating potential for distributed deep learning if sustained beyond individual initiatives.

signals.title: Virginia Tech sets course for human-centered AI leadership - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's commitment to human-centered AI leadership positions a non-NoVA institution as a potential knowledge distribution hub, creating infrastructure for peer learning networks across regions if extended beyond campus boundaries.

signals.title: Camp Welcomes Hampton Roads Youth to Learn About Cybersecurity and AI - Old Dominion University
signals.signal_reading: Youth-focused cybersecurity and AI camps at ODU demonstrate early-stage capability development in a military-adjacent region, building foundational fluency that could distribute technical depth beyond traditional tech hubs.

signals.title: Column: For rural Virginia, data centers are more than technology - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Data centers arriving in rural Virginia primarily signal infrastructure concentration without local capability transfer—jobs and economic impact remain shallow unless accompanied by workforce development that builds genuine AI fluency.

signals.title: Roanoke College joins Google AI for Education Accelerator - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's partnership with Google's AI Accelerator suggests platform-mediated adoption rather than indigenous capability building, potentially creating broad but shallow usage dependent on external corporate tools.
